title.zh: 卷397 列傳一百八十四 陆建瀛 杨文定 青麟 崇纶 何桂清
title.en: Volume 397 Biographies 184: Lu Jianying, Yang Wending, Qing Lin, Chong Lun, He Guiqing
title.raw: 卷397 列傳一百八十四 陆建瀛 杨文定 青麟 崇纶 何桂清

sentences.zh: =陸建瀛=陸建瀛，字立夫，湖北沔陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Jianying, styled Lifu, was a native of Mianyang in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jianying (style name Lifu) was from Mianyang, Hubei.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，直上書房，洊遷中允。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, served in the Upper Study, and was promoted in due course to vice chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Daoguang 2 (1822), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed a compiler in the Upper Study, and rose step by step to vice chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 大考擢侍講，轉侍讀。

translations.literal: In the great examination he was promoted to attendant lecturer, then transferred to attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: After the triennial palace examination he was promoted to attendant lecturer and then transferred to attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 二十年，出為直隸天津道，累擢布政使。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he went out as Daotai of Zhili Tianjin, and was promoted in succession to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 20 (1840) he left the capital to serve as Tianjin circuit intendant in Zhili, and was eventually promoted to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 時英吉利擾浙江，沿海戒嚴，徵西北兵聚畿輔，建瀛供防軍，處善後，皆應機宜。

translations.literal: At the time England disturbed Zhejiang, the coast was placed under strict guard, troops from the northwest were summoned to gather in the capital region, and Jianying supplied the defense armies and handled aftermath matters, all in keeping with the needs of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: When Britain was raiding Zhejiang and the coast was on high alert, northwestern troops were called in to concentrate around the capital. Jianying provisioned the defense forces and handled relief and recovery, each measure suited to circumstances.

sentences.zh: 所歷有名績。

translations.literal: In every post he held he had noted achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he left a distinguished record.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢雲南巡撫，俄調江蘇。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to governor of Yunnan, and soon transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 26 (1846) he was made governor of Yunnan, then shortly transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 先是，南漕缺額，部議設局江蘇，官民捐米運京以裕倉儲。

translations.literal: Previously, the southern tribute grain quota fell short, and the ministry proposed establishing an office in Jiangsu whereby officials and people would donate grain to transport to the capital in order to replenish the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, shortfalls in southern tribute grain had led the ministry to propose a Jiangsu office through which officials and commoners would donate rice for shipment to Beijing to fill the state granaries.

sentences.zh: 當陶澍撫蘇，即以漕河費鉅病國，議行海運，官吏爭撓之，暫行輒罷。

translations.literal: When Tao Shu governed Jiangsu, he had already held that the huge cost of the grain canal was draining the state and proposed sea transport, but officials in succession obstructed it, and whenever it was tried it was soon halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Shu was governor of Jiangsu he had argued that the enormous cost of the Grand Canal was crippling the treasury and pushed for shipping grain by sea, but officials repeatedly blocked the plan and every trial was quickly abandoned.

sentences.zh: 至是建瀛與兩江總督壁昌主海運甚力，合言其便，議蘇州、松江、太倉白糧改由海運，從之。

translations.literal: At this time Jianying and the Liangjiang governor-general Bi Chang strongly advocated sea transport, jointly stating its convenience, and proposed that the white rice of Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang be changed to sea transport; the proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jianying and Liangjiang governor-general Bi Chang pressed hard for coastal shipping, jointly argued its advantages, and proposed that white-grain tribute from Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang go by sea; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 後復推至常、鎮諸府。

translations.literal: Later it was extended further to Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The arrangement was later extended to Changzhou, Zhenjiang, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，廷臣會議南漕改折，建瀛與總督李星沅極言其窒礙，事遂不行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the court ministers met to discuss converting southern tribute grain to a money commutation; Jianying and Governor Li Xingyuan strongly stated its obstructiveness, and the matter thereupon did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 29 (1849) when ministers debated converting southern grain tribute into a cash levy, Jianying and Governor Li Xingyuan argued forcefully that the scheme would be unworkable, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 擢兩江總督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Liangjiang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor-general of Liangjiang.

sentences.zh: 值大水，民飢，招徠米商，籌議撫卹，並疏消積水，請籌撥帑一百五十萬備賑。

translations.literal: There came great floods, the people were hungry, he summoned grain merchants, planned relief and consolation, and also petitioned to drain accumulated floodwater, requesting an allocation of 1.5 million taels from the treasury for famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy flooding left the populace starving; he drew in rice merchants, organized relief, petitioned to drain standing water, and asked for 1.5 million taels from the treasury for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 吳城六堡河決阻​​運，命偕侍郎福濟往勘，疏陳通籌湖、河大勢，添塘避徬，對壩逼溜，攻刷海口各事宜，並如議行。

translations.literal: The Liubao River at Wucheng burst its banks and blocked transport; he was ordered to go with Vice Minister Fu Ji to survey the damage, and in a memorial set forth the overall plan for coordinating lakes and rivers, adding embankments to avoid oblique currents, facing dikes against rushing water, scouring the estuary mouth, and other matters, all of which were carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liubao River at Wucheng broke its banks and blocked the canal, he was sent with Vice Minister Fu Ji to inspect the site. His memorial outlined a comprehensive plan for lakes and rivers—adding dikes to divert sideways currents, aligning embankments against the main flow, scouring the estuary—and the court implemented his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 淮鹽積敝，自陶澍創改淮北為票鹽，稍稍蘇息；

translations.literal: The Huai salt trade had accumulated abuses; since Tao Shu pioneered changing northern Huai to ticket salt, it gradually revived;
translations.idiomatic: Corruption had long plagued the Huai salt monopoly; after Tao Shu introduced ticket-based salt in northern Huai the trade slowly recovered;

sentences.zh: 而淮南擅鹽利久，官吏衣食於鹽商，無肯議改者，建瀛悉其弊。

translations.literal: but in southern Huai the salt monopoly had long been monopolized for profit, officials and clerks lived off the salt merchants, and none were willing to discuss reform; Jianying was fully aware of its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: yet southern Huai salt interests had been entrenched for generations, officials and clerks depended on salt merchants for their livelihood, and no one would broach reform—though Jianying knew every abuse.

sentences.zh: 會淮南鹽大火於武昌，官商折閱數百萬，課大虧，引滯庫絀。

translations.literal: It happened that Huai salt stores in Wuchang caught a great fire, officials and merchants suffered losses of several million, the revenue was greatly depleted, salt certificates stagnated and the treasury was drained.
translations.idiomatic: When a major fire destroyed Huai salt warehouses at Wuchang, merchants and the state lost millions, revenue collapsed, transport permits piled up idle, and the treasury was strained.

sentences.zh: 三十年，乃疏請立限清查運庫，並統籌淮南大局，改訂新章十條，務在以輕本敵私，力裁繁文浮費。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he thereupon memorialized requesting a time limit for thorough investigation of the transport granaries, and coordinating the overall southern Huai situation, revising ten new regulations, aiming to lighten capital costs to compete with private salt and vigorously cut redundant paperwork and inflated expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 30 (1850) he petitioned for a deadline to audit transport granaries, presented a comprehensive southern Huai reform, and issued ten new regulations aimed at lowering costs to undercut private salt and slash bureaucratic waste.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺少卿劉良駒亦請變通淮南舊章，仿淮北行票法，與建瀛所議同。

translations.literal: Liu Liangju, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, also requested adapting the old southern Huai regulations and imitating northern Huai in implementing the ticket method, the same as Jianying's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liangju of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices likewise urged revising southern Huai rules along northern Huai ticket-salt lines, aligning with Jianying's plan.

sentences.zh: 方施行矣，而給事中曹履泰奏請復根窩舊制，御史周炳鑑言淮南改票不便，並下建瀛議。

translations.literal: Just as it was being implemented, supervising secretary Cao Lütai memorialized requesting restoration of the old root-nest system, censor Zhou Bingjian stated that changing southern Huai to tickets was inconvenient, and both were referred to Jianying for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Implementation had just begun when Supervising Secretary Cao Lütai petitioned to restore the old registered-nest system and Censor Zhou Bingjian argued that ticket salt would not work in southern Huai; both memorials were sent to Jianying for reply.

sentences.zh: 覆疏辨駁詳至，文宗韙之，詔綜斡全局，除弊興利，以裨國計。

translations.literal: In his reply memorial he rebutted in full detail; Emperor Wenzong approved it, and edicted him to coordinate the overall situation, remove abuses and promote benefits, to benefit state finance.
translations.idiomatic: Jianying's detailed reply won Emperor Wenzong's approval; he was ordered to take charge of the whole reform, cut abuses, and strengthen state revenue.

sentences.zh: 建瀛議於揚州設局收納，以清運署需索之源；

translations.literal: Jianying proposed establishing a collection office at Yangzhou to clear away the source of demands from the transport bureau;
translations.idiomatic: Jianying proposed a collection office at Yangzhou to eliminate extortion by the transport bureau;

sentences.zh: 於九江等處驗發，以清楚西岸費之源。

translations.literal: and inspection and issuance at Jiujiang and other places, to clear away the source of western-bank fees.
translations.idiomatic: and inspection and issuance at Jiujiang and elsewhere to cut off illicit western-bank charges.

sentences.zh: 正雜錢糧並納，則課額不虧；

translations.literal: if regular and miscellaneous taxes were paid together, then the revenue quota would not fall short;
translations.idiomatic: if regular and miscellaneous levies were paid together, revenue quotas would be met;

sentences.zh: 新舊商販一體，則引額無缺。

translations.literal: if new and old merchants were treated alike, then certificate quotas would not be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: if new and established merchants were treated equally, transport permits would not go unfilled.

sentences.zh: 灶私場私，專責江南；

translations.literal: furnace smuggling and depot smuggling would be the sole responsibility of Jiangnan;
translations.idiomatic: smuggling at salt furnaces and depots would be Jiangnan's responsibility alone;

sentences.zh: 江私鄰私，兼責各省；

translations.literal: river smuggling and neighboring smuggling would be the joint responsibility of the various provinces;
translations.idiomatic: smuggling on the river and in neighboring provinces would be shared among the provinces;

sentences.zh: 而以徠商販，積帑賦，自總其成。

translations.literal: and by attracting merchants, accumulating treasury revenue, he would himself oversee the whole.
translations.idiomatic: and he would personally oversee attracting merchants and building up treasury revenue.

sentences.zh: 由是奪官吏中飽歲百餘萬，惎謗叢作，建瀛銳自發舒，不之卹。

translations.literal: Thereby he took from officials' annual illicit gains of more than a million, slander arose in clusters, but Jianying pressed forward boldly and did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: This stripped officials of more than a million taels in annual graft; slander poured in, but Jianying pushed ahead without concern.

sentences.zh: 朝廷信任益專，命有掣肘撓法者罪之。

translations.literal: The court's trust in him grew ever more exclusive, and it ordered that whoever obstructed or interfered with the law should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The court placed ever greater trust in him and ordered that anyone who obstructed the reforms be punished.

sentences.zh: 湖北鹽道鄒之玉沿用整輪，江西鹽道慶雲強索月給，湖北同知勞光泰作移岸三論，刊板傳播，並劾罷之。

translations.literal: Zou Zhiyu, Hubei salt intendant, continued the whole-round practice; Qing Yun, Jiangxi salt intendant, forcibly demanded monthly payments; Lao Guangtai, Hubei subprefect, wrote the Three Discourses on Shore Transfer, had them printed and circulated—and all were impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and dismissed Hubei salt intendant Zou Zhiyu for clinging to the whole-round system, Jiangxi salt intendant Qing Yun for demanding monthly bribes, and Hubei subprefect Lao Guangtai for publishing his Three Discourses on Shore Transfer.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，河決豐北，命建瀛往勘，奏請以工代賑，偕南河總督楊以增督工。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng the Yellow River burst its banks at Fengbei; Jianying was ordered to go survey it, memorialized requesting relief through labor, and together with Southern Rivers governor-general Yang Yizeng supervised the works.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 1 (1851) when the Yellow River broke at Fengbei, Jianying was sent to inspect the breach, proposed work-for-relief, and supervised repairs with Southern Rivers governor-general Yang Yizeng.

sentences.zh: 二年，以盛漲停工，降四品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the second year, because of high flood the work was halted, and he was demoted to fourth-rank hat button.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 (1852) work was suspended during high water and his hat button was reduced to fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，粵匪洪秀全犯湖南，越洞庭而北，勢張甚。

translations.literal: That autumn the Cantonese rebels under Hong Xiuquan invaded Hunan, crossed Dongting northward, and their momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Taiping leader Hong Xiuquan invaded Hunan, crossed Lake Dongting northward, and his forces were surging.

sentences.zh: 建瀛猶在豐工，疏上戰守事宜，文宗嘉之，諭以審度軍情，如須親往，可速籌方略，不遙制。

translations.literal: Jianying was still at the Fengbei works; he memorialized on offensive and defensive matters, and Wenzong commended him, instructing him to assess the military situation, and if he needed to go in person, to quickly plan strategy without remote control from the court.
translations.idiomatic: Jianying was still at Fengbei when he submitted a memorial on strategy; Wenzong praised it and told him to judge the military situation himself—if he needed to take the field, to plan quickly without waiting for orders from Beijing.

sentences.zh: 既而漢陽、武昌相繼陷。

translations.literal: Before long Hanyang and Wuchang fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hanyang and Wuchang fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 十二月，復建瀛頭品頂戴，授欽差大臣，督師赴九江上游扼守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jianying's first-rank hat button was restored, he was appointed imperial commissioner, and ordered to lead troops to the upper reaches of Jiujiang to hold the line.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month his first-rank hat button was restored, he was made imperial commissioner, and sent to command troops at the upper Yangtze above Jiujiang to block the rebels.

sentences.zh: 建瀛由工次還江寧，徵調倉猝。

translations.literal: Jianying returned from the works to Jiangning, and the levy and deployment were hasty.
translations.idiomatic: Jianying returned from the river works to Nanjing and mobilized troops in great haste.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，賊棄武昌，蔽江東下，建瀛欲行，或謂賊鋒銳難驟當，建瀛尚輕之，檄壽春鎮總兵恩長為翼長，領標兵二千當前鋒，自率兵千餘進次九江。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the rebels abandoned Wuchang and swept down the river; Jianying wished to advance, but some said the rebels' edge was sharp and hard to meet at once; Jianying still underestimated them, ordered Shouchun garrison commander En Chang as wing commander with two thousand banner troops as vanguard, and himself led more than a thousand troops to advance and encamp at Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xianfeng 3 (1853) the rebels left Wuchang and swept downriver. Jianying meant to engage them; others warned that the rebel spearhead was too sharp to meet head-on, but he still underestimated them. He appointed Shouchun garrison commander En Chang wing commander with two thousand banner troops as vanguard and advanced to Jiujiang with a little over a thousand men of his own.

sentences.zh: 恩長猝與賊，戰死江中，師大潰。

translations.literal: En Chang suddenly encountered the rebels, was killed in battle on the river, and the army collapsed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: En Chang suddenly clashed with the rebels, was killed on the river, and the army routed completely.

sentences.zh: 建瀛途逢潰卒白敗狀，從兵盡駭。

translations.literal: Jianying met fleeing soldiers on the road who reported the defeat; his accompanying troops were all terrified.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Jianying met fleeing soldiers who told him of the defeat, and his escort was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 江西巡撫張芾壁九江，亦引軍退走，賊遂陷九江。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Governor Zhang Fu had fortified Jiujiang, but also withdrew his army and fled, and the rebels thereupon took Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi governor Zhang Fu had fortified Jiujiang but also retreated, and the rebels captured the city.

sentences.zh: 建瀛駕小舟經小孤山不敢留，過安慶，巡撫蔣文慶邀之，不入；

translations.literal: Jianying took a small boat past Xiaogu Mountain and dared not stop; passing Anqing, Governor Jiang Wenqing invited him in, but he did not enter;
translations.idiomatic: Jianying took a small boat past Xiaogu Mountain without daring to stop; at Anqing, Governor Jiang Wenqing invited him ashore, but he refused;

sentences.zh: 徑回江寧，收蕪湖、太平兵屯東西梁山，閉城為守禦計。

translations.literal: he went straight back to Jiangning, gathered troops from Wuhu and Taiping to encamp at the Eastern and Western Liang Mountains, and closed the city as a plan for defense.
translations.idiomatic: he went straight back to Nanjing, gathered troops from Wuhu and Taiping to camp at the Eastern and Western Liang Mountains, and shut the city gates to prepare a defense.

sentences.zh: 布政使祁宿藻故不滿建瀛，面責之。

translations.literal: Provincial administration commissioner Qi Suzao had long been dissatisfied with Jianying and rebuked him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial administration commissioner Qi Suzao, who had long disliked Jianying, rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 將軍祥厚兵防內城，無任戰守者。

translations.literal: General Xianghou kept troops to defend the inner city, and no one was responsible for fighting or holding the line.
translations.idiomatic: General Xianghou kept his troops to defend the inner city, and no one took charge of the outer defenses.

sentences.zh: 建瀛大窘，稱疾謝客者三日。

translations.literal: Jianying was greatly embarrassed and for three days claimed illness and refused visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly humiliated, Jianying claimed illness and refused visitors for three days.

sentences.zh: 於是祥厚、宿藻等疏劾建瀛棄險失機，進退無據，並及江蘇巡撫楊文定違旨去江寧，上大怒，諭曰：「陸建瀛一戰兵潰，不知收合餘燼，與向榮大軍協力攻擊；

translations.literal: Thereupon Xianghou, Suzao, and others memorialized impeaching Jianying for abandoning strategic points and missing opportunities, advancing and retreating without basis, and also involving Jiangsu Governor Yang Wending for leaving Jiangning against orders; the emperor was greatly angered and instructed: "Lu Jianying's army collapsed in one battle, yet he did not know how to gather the remaining embers and join Xiang Rong's great army in a concerted attack;
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou, Suzao, and others then impeached Jianying for abandoning key positions, missing his chance, and acting without plan, and also accused Jiangsu governor Yang Wending of leaving Nanjing against orders. The emperor was furious and declared: "After one battle Lu Jianying's troops routed, yet he did not rally the survivors to join Xiang Rong's main force in a coordinated attack;

sentences.zh: 並不力守小孤山，扼賊入皖之路；

translations.literal: nor did he vigorously hold Xiaogu Mountain to block the rebels' route into Anhui;
translations.idiomatic: nor did he hold Xiaogu Mountain to block the rebels' path into Anhui;

sentences.zh: 又不親督兵據守東西梁山，以障金陵。

translations.literal: nor did he personally lead troops to hold the Eastern and Western Liang Mountains to shield Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: nor did he personally command troops at the Eastern and Western Liang Mountains to shield Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 倉皇遁歸，一籌莫​​展，以致會垣驚擾，士民播遷。

translations.literal: He fled back in panic, could not devise a single plan, so that the provincial capital was thrown into alarm and officials and people were scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: He fled back in panic without a single plan, throwing the provincial capital into turmoil and driving officials and commoners to scatter.

sentences.zh: 楊文定藉詞出省，張皇自全，罪均難逭。

translations.literal: Yang Wending used pretexts to leave the province and in panic saved himself alone; their crimes alike could not be escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wending used excuses to leave the province and saved himself in panic; both men's crimes were beyond excuse.

sentences.zh: 建瀛已革職，交祥厚拿問，解刑部治罪。」

translations.literal: Jianying was already dismissed from office, handed over to Xianghou for arrest and interrogation, and sent to the Ministry of Justice for punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Jianying was dismissed, handed to Xianghou for arrest, and sent to the Ministry of Justice for trial."

sentences.zh: 尋籍其家，革其子刑部員外郎鍾漢職。

translations.literal: Soon his household was confiscated, and his son Zhong Han, a secretary in the Ministry of Justice, was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: His property was soon confiscated and his son Zhong Han, a secretary in the Ministry of Justice, was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 時建瀛收兵乘城，閱十三日，城破遇害。

translations.literal: At the time Jianying had gathered troops and manned the walls; after thirteen days the city fell and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jianying had rallied troops onto the walls; after thirteen days the city fell and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔建瀛尚不失城亡與亡之義，复總督銜，如例議卹，並還其家產。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict stated that Jianying had not lost the principle of perishing with the city when it fell, restored his governor-general rank, granted posthumous honors according to precedent, and returned his household property.
translations.idiomatic: When news arrived, the court ruled that Jianying had not failed the duty of dying with his city, restored his governor-general rank, granted standard posthumous honors, and returned his property.

sentences.zh: 御史方俊論之，乃撤卹典。

translations.literal: Censor Fang Jun argued against it, and the posthumous honors were thereupon withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fang Jun protested, and the posthumous honors were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 建瀛才敏任事，喜賓禮名流，又善事要津，多為延譽，由是聞望猋起，朝寄日隆。

translations.literal: Jianying was talented and quick in affairs, delighted in treating famous men as guests, and was also good at cultivating key figures; many praised him, and thereby his reputation soared and the court's reliance on him grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Jianying was clever and energetic, entertained eminent scholars, cultivated men of influence, and won widespread praise—his reputation soared and the court's confidence in him deepened.

sentences.zh: 乃昧於軍旅，略無宿備，一敗失措，名城陷為賊窟，糜爛東南，遂獨攖天下之重咎雲。

translations.literal: Yet he was ignorant of military affairs, had virtually no prior preparations, and after one defeat lost his composure; a famous city fell and became a rebel nest, the southeast was ravaged, and he alone bore the heavy blame of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he knew nothing of war, made no real preparations, and after one defeat lost his nerve; a great city became a rebel stronghold, the southeast was laid waste, and he alone bore the nation's heaviest blame.

sentences.zh: 子鍾漢，後官江蘇知府，咸豐十年，在軍治糧餉，遇賊江陰，死之，贈太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: His son Zhong Han later served as prefect of Jiangsu; in the tenth year of Xianfeng, while in the army managing grain supplies, he encountered rebels at Jiangyin and died, and was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong Han later became prefect of Jiangsu; in Xianfeng 10 (1860), while managing army provisions, he was killed by rebels at Jiangyin and was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: =楊文定=楊文定，安徽定遠人。

translations.literal: Yang Wending was a native of Dingyuan in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wending was from Dingyuan, Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Daoguang 13 (1833).

sentences.zh: 由刑部主事洊升郎中，出為廣東惠潮嘉道，累擢江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: From a clerk in the Ministry of Justice he was promoted in due course to director, went out as Daotai of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiaxing in Guangdong, and was promoted in succession to governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from clerk to director in the Ministry of Justice, served as intendant of the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiaxing circuit in Guangdong, and was eventually promoted to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，文定奏江南兵力柔脆，節經徵調，城內兵單，請濟師，命山東兵二千赴援。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng Wending memorialized that Jiangnan troops were soft and weak, had been repeatedly levied, and troops in the city were few; he requested reinforcements, and two thousand Shandong troops were ordered to aid.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 (1853) Wending reported that Jiangnan troops were weak and depleted by repeated levies, that Nanjing was undermanned, and asked for reinforcements; two thousand Shandong troops were ordered to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 未至，奉命守江寧，聞建瀛兵敗，退守鎮江。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, he was ordered to defend Jiangning; hearing of Jianying's defeat, he withdrew to defend Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived he was ordered to hold Nanjing; when he heard of Jianying's defeat he fell back to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 江寧陷，賊分黨犯鎮江，副都統文藝集兵七百守陸路，文定自率艇船八、舢板十二泊江中，賊至不能禦，鎮江复陷，退江陰，詔革職逮治，論大辟。

translations.literal: When Jiangning fell, the rebels sent a division to attack Zhenjiang; Vice Commander Wen Yi gathered seven hundred troops to defend the land route, while Wending himself led eight gunboats and twelve sampans moored on the river; when the rebels arrived they could not resist, Zhenjiang again fell, and he retreated to Jiangyin; an edict dismissed him from office for arrest and trial, sentencing him to death.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjing fell the rebels sent a column against Zhenjiang. Vice commander Wen Yi gathered seven hundred men for the land defense while Wending led eight gunboats and twelve sampans on the river. They could not hold; Zhenjiang fell again and he retreated to Jiangyin. The court dismissed him, ordered his arrest, and sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 六年，減死遣戍軍台，尋歿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his death sentence was commuted and he was sent to garrison the military colonies; he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 6 (1856) his sentence was commuted to exile at the military colonies, where he soon died.

sentences.zh: =青麟=青麟，字墨卿，圖們氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Qing Lin, styled Moqing, of the Tumen clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Lin (style name Moqing), of the Tumen clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷中允。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and promoted to vice chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Daoguang 21 (1841), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed compiler, and rose to vice chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 大考二等，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the great examination he placed second class and was promoted to attendant lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the triennial palace examination he placed second class and was promoted to attendant lecturer.

sentences.zh: 五遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he reached Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 督江蘇學政有聲。

translations.literal: As educational commissioner of Jiangsu he had a notable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: As Jiangsu educational commissioner he won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was promoted to vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 (1852) he was promoted to vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 學政任滿，命督催豐北塞決工程。

translations.literal: When his term as educational commissioner ended, he was ordered to supervise and urge the Fengbei breach-closing project.
translations.idiomatic: When his term as educational commissioner ended, he was ordered to oversee the Fengbei breach repair.

sentences.zh: 三年，回京，復出督湖北學政，調禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he returned to the capital, then went out again as educational commissioner of Hubei, and was transferred to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 (1853) he returned to Beijing, then went out again as Hubei educational commissioner and was transferred to vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪由江西回竄湖北，青麟按試德安，聞警停試，督率知府易容之募鄉勇籌防守，府城獲全。

translations.literal: At the time the Cantonese rebels from Jiangxi swept back into Hubei; Qing Lin was conducting examinations at De'an, heard the alarm and halted the tests, supervised and led Prefect Yi Rongzhi in recruiting local militia and planning defense, and the prefectural city was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiping forces from Jiangxi swept back into Hubei, Qing Lin was holding examinations at De'an. He halted the tests at the first alarm, worked with prefect Yi Rongzhi to raise local militia, and kept the prefectural city intact.

sentences.zh: 疏陳軍事，請湖北、江西、安徽三省合剿，以期得力。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth military affairs and requested that Hubei, Jiangxi, and Anhui jointly suppress the rebels in the hope of effective results.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on military affairs and urged a joint campaign by Hubei, Jiangxi, and Anhui to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 四年，授湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 4 (1854) he was appointed governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 城中兵僅千人，荊州將軍台湧署總督，未至；

translations.literal: Troops in the city numbered only a thousand; Jingzhou General Tai Yong was acting governor-general, but had not yet arrived;
translations.idiomatic: The city had barely a thousand troops; Jingzhou general Tai Yong was acting governor-general but had not yet arrived;

sentences.zh: 而賊由黃州進至漢陽、漢口，渡江欲撲武昌。

translations.literal: while the rebels advanced from Huangzhou to Hanyang and Hankou, crossed the river intending to storm Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: while rebels advanced from Huangzhou to Hanyang and Hankou and crossed the river to strike Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 青麟督總兵楊昌泗、游擊侯鳳岐與副都統魁玉水陸合擊，卻之；

translations.literal: Qing Lin supervised Brigadier Yang Changsi, Colonel Hou Fengqi, and Vice Commander Kui Yu in a combined land and water attack and repelled them;
translations.idiomatic: Qing Lin directed brigadier Yang Changsi, colonel Hou Fengqi, and vice commander Kui Yu in a combined land-and-water assault and drove them back;

sentences.zh: 复敗之豹子海、魯家港，毀賊壘五。

translations.literal: again defeated them at Baozihai and Lujiagang, destroying five rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: then defeated them again at Baozihai and Lujiagang and destroyed five rebel camps.

sentences.zh: 已而賊撲塘角、鮎魚套，逼攻省城，青麟武勝門督戰，城中忽火起，土匪內應，兵盡潰，遂失守。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels attacked Tangjiao and Nianyutao and pressed the provincial city; Qing Lin directed the fighting at Wusheng Gate; suddenly fire broke out in the city, local bandits responded from within, the troops collapsed entirely, and the city was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels struck Tangjiao and Nianyutao and pressed the provincial capital. Qing Lin commanded at Wusheng Gate, but fire suddenly broke out in the city, local bandits rose inside, the army routed completely, and Wuchang fell.

sentences.zh: 青麟將自經，眾擁之趨長沙，折赴荊州。

translations.literal: Qing Lin was about to hang himself, but the crowd escorted him toward Changsha, then he turned and went to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Lin was about to take his own life, but his followers hustled him toward Changsha; he then turned aside for Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，文宗聞其出家貲犒軍，甚嘉之，至是憤武昌屢失，棄城越境，罪尤重，詔曰：「青麟簡任封圻，正當賊匪充斥，武昌兵單餉匱。

translations.literal: Earlier Wenzong had heard that he spent his own family wealth to reward the troops and greatly commended him; now, enraged that Wuchang had repeatedly fallen and that he had abandoned the city and crossed borders, his crime was especially grave, and an edict stated: "Qing Lin was specially appointed to a frontier post just when rebels were everywhere, Wuchang had few troops and scant supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wenzong had praised him for spending family wealth to reward the troops; now, furious that Wuchang had fallen repeatedly and that he had abandoned his post and fled across provincial borders, the emperor declared his crime especially grave: "Qing Lin was specially appointed to a frontier post just as rebels swarmed everywhere; Wuchang had few troops and scant supplies.

sentences.zh: 朕以其任學政時保守德安，念其勤勞，畀以重任。

translations.literal: We, remembering that during his term as educational commissioner he preserved De'an, mindful of his diligence, entrusted him with a heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering how he had held De'an during his term as educational commissioner, I rewarded his diligence with a weighty appointment.

sentences.zh: 省垣佈置，屢次擊賊獲勝。

translations.literal: His arrangements at the provincial capital repeatedly defeated the rebels with victories.
translations.idiomatic: His dispositions at the provincial capital repeatedly beat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 八十餘日之中，困苦艱難，所奏原無虛假，朕方嚴催援兵接應。

translations.literal: Within more than eighty days of hardship and difficulty, what he reported was not false; We were urgently pressing reinforcements to link up with him.
translations.idiomatic: For more than eighty days of hardship his reports were not false, and I was urgently pressing reinforcements to reach him.

sentences.zh: 六月初間，魁​​玉、楊昌泗等連破賊營，但能激厲力戰，何致遽陷？

translations.literal: In early the sixth month Kui Yu, Yang Changsi, and others repeatedly broke rebel camps; if only he had roused them to fight hard, how could it have fallen so quickly?
translations.idiomatic: In early the sixth month Kui Yu and Yang Changsi had repeatedly smashed rebel camps—had he only roused them to fight hard, how could the city have fallen so suddenly?

sentences.zh: 嬰城固守，解圍有日，猶將宥過論功。

translations.literal: If he had held the city firmly in siege, relief would have come in time, and We would still have pardoned faults and reckoned merit.
translations.idiomatic: Had he held the city under siege, relief would have come in time and I would still have overlooked faults and counted his service.

sentences.zh: 縱力盡捐軀，褒忠有典，豈不心跡光明？

translations.literal: Even if he had exhausted his strength and given his life, there are precedents for honoring loyalty—would not his heart and conduct have been clear?
translations.idiomatic: Even if he had exhausted his strength and given his life, precedents for honoring loyalty exist—would not his conduct have been beyond reproach?

sentences.zh: 乃倉皇遠避，徑赴長沙，直是棄城而逃。

translations.literal: Yet he fled far away in panic, went straight to Changsha—it was plainly abandoning the city and fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he fled in panic straight to Changsha—nothing less than abandoning his city and running away.

sentences.zh: 長沙非所轄之地，越境偷生，何詞以解？

translations.literal: Changsha was not within his jurisdiction; crossing borders to save his own life—what words could excuse it?
translations.idiomatic: Changsha was outside his jurisdiction; by crossing borders to save himself, what excuse could he offer?

sentences.zh: 若再加寬典，是疆臣守土之責，幾成具文，何以對死事諸臣耶！

translations.literal: If We were to grant further leniency, the duty of frontier officials to hold their territory would become empty words—how could We face the officials who died in service?
translations.idiomatic: If I showed further leniency, the duty of frontier officials to hold their ground would become a dead letter—how could I face the officials who died in service?

sentences.zh: 朕賞罰一秉大公，豈能以前此微勞，稍從末減？

translations.literal: Our rewards and punishments rest entirely on public justice—how could We, because of his slight earlier service, reduce the penalty in the least?
translations.idiomatic: My rewards and punishments rest on justice alone—how could his slight earlier service win him any reduction?

sentences.zh: 俟到荊州時，交官文傳旨正法。」

translations.literal: When he reaches Jingzhou, hand him over to Guanwen to convey the edict and execute the law."
translations.idiomatic: When he reaches Jingzhou, Guanwen is to convey the edict and execute him."

sentences.zh: 遂棄市。

translations.literal: He was thereupon executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He was then executed in public.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，曾國籓复武昌，奉命查歷任督撫功罪，疏言：「武昌再陷，實因崇綸、台湧多方貽誤，百姓恨之，極稱吳文鎔忠勤愛國，於青麟亦多恕辭。

translations.literal: After several months Zeng Guofan recovered Wuchang and was ordered to investigate the merits and faults of successive governors-general and governors; he memorialized: "Wuchang's second fall was truly due to Chong Lun and Tai Yong causing harm in many ways; the people hated them and greatly praised Wu Wenrong's loyal diligence and love of country, while toward Qing Lin they also spoke many words of forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Zeng Guofan retook Wuchang and was ordered to review the record of successive governors. He reported: "Wuchang's second fall was chiefly due to Chong Lun and Tai Yong, whom the people hated; they praised Wu Wenrong's loyal service, and spoke forgivingly even of Qing Lin.

sentences.zh: 查文鎔既沒，青麟幫辦軍務，崇綸百端齟《齒吾》：求弁兵以護衛，不與；

translations.literal: Investigation shows that after Wenrong died, Qing Lin assisted in military affairs, while Chong Lun obstructed in a hundred ways: he requested guards for his protection and was refused;
translations.idiomatic: After Wenrong's death Qing Lin helped manage military affairs, while Chong Lun obstructed him at every turn—he asked for guards and was refused;

sentences.zh: 請銀兩以製械，不與；

translations.literal: he requested silver taels to manufacture weapons and was refused;
translations.idiomatic: he asked for funds to make arms and was refused;

sentences.zh: 或軍務不使聞知，或經旬不得相見。

translations.literal: at times he was kept from hearing of military affairs, or for ten-day spans they could not meet;
translations.idiomatic: sometimes military affairs were kept from him, sometimes they would not meet for weeks;

sentences.zh: 自賊踞漢陽、漢口，縱橫蹂躪，廬舍蕩然。

translations.literal: since the rebels held Hanyang and Hankou, they rampaged across the land until dwellings were utterly swept away;
translations.idiomatic: once the rebels held Hanyang and Hankou they ravaged the region until homes were utterly destroyed;

sentences.zh: 百姓尚恃有青麟督兵驅逐，出示憐民。

translations.literal: the people still relied on Qing Lin supervising troops to drive them out and issuing proclamations showing compassion for the populace;
translations.idiomatic: the people still counted on Qing Lin to lead troops against them and issue benevolent proclamations;

sentences.zh: 崇綸則並此無之矣。」

translations.literal: as for Chong Lun, he had not even this;"
translations.idiomatic: Chong Lun did none of this;"

sentences.zh: 疏入，乃斥罷台湧，論崇綸罪。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Tai Yong was dismissed and Chong Lun's crimes were adjudicated.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Tai Yong was dismissed and Chong Lun was put on trial.

sentences.zh: =崇綸=崇綸，喜塔臘氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Chong Lun, of the Xitala clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Lun (Xitala clan) was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 由內閣貼寫中書充軍機章京，洊升侍讀。

translations.literal: From a Grand Secretariat copyist-attendant secretary he served as a Grand Council clerk and was repeatedly promoted to attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from a Grand Secretariat copyist to Grand Council clerk and was promoted to attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 出為陝西鳳邠道，調直隸永定河道，歷雲南按察使、廣東布政使。

translations.literal: He went out as Feng-Bin circuit intendant in Shaanxi, was transferred to Yongding River commissioner in Zhili, and successively served as Yunnan surveillance commissioner and Guangdong provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Feng-Bin circuit intendant in Shaanxi, was transferred to Yongding River commissioner in Zhili, and later became Yunnan surveillance commissioner and Guangdong provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，擢湖北巡撫，時武昌方為賊踞，次年春，賊棄武漢東下，分擾江南、江西，崇綸始抵任。

translations.literal: In Xianfeng 2 (1852) he was promoted to Hubei governor; Wuchang was still held by rebels, and the following spring when they abandoned Wuhan and marched east to harass Jiangnan and Jiangxi, Chong Lun only then reached his post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he was made Hubei governor while Wuchang was still in rebel hands; the next spring the rebels left Wuhan and marched east into Jiangnan and Jiangxi, and Chong Lun only then took up his post.

sentences.zh: 既而賊复上竄，陷興國州田家鎮，進黃州。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels again drove upstream, took Tianjiazhen in Xingguo prefecture, and advanced on Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels drove north again, took Tianjiazhen in Xingguo, and advanced on Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇綸疏言：「武漢民遷市絕，餉乏兵單。

translations.literal: Chong Lun memorialized: "In Wuhan the people have fled and markets are cut off; rations are short and troops few.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Lun wrote: "Wuhan's people have fled and trade has stopped; supplies are scarce and troops few.

sentences.zh: 請移內就外，以剿為先。」

translations.literal: I beg to shift inward toward outward action and make suppression the priority."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to move from defense inward to pursuit outward and put suppression first."

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊犯漢陽，窺武昌。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels attacked Hanyang and menaced Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels struck Hanyang and threatened Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 總督吳文鎔初至，與崇綸意相迕。

translations.literal: Governor-general Wu Wenrong had just arrived, and his views clashed with Chong Lun's.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Wu Wenrong had just arrived and clashed with Chong Lun at every turn.

sentences.zh: 及賊退，崇綸遂以閉城株守劾之。

translations.literal: When the rebels retreated, Chong Lun memorialized to impeach him for shutting the city and holding static defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew, Chong Lun impeached him for shutting the gates and holding a passive defense.

sentences.zh: 文宗慮兩人不能和衷，且僨事，命文鎔出剿，而責崇綸防守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong worried the two could not cooperate harmoniously and would ruin affairs; he ordered Wenrong out to suppress while holding Chong Lun responsible for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong feared they could not work together and would ruin the campaign; he sent Wenrong out to fight and charged Chong Lun with defense.

sentences.zh: 文鎔率師薄黃州，崇綸運輸餉械不以時，惟促速戰。

translations.literal: Wenrong led troops to press Huangzhou; Chong Lun did not deliver supplies and weapons on time but only urged rapid battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wenrong led his army toward Huangzhou, but Chong Lun failed to deliver pay and arms on schedule and only pressed him to fight quickly.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，文鎔兵敗，死之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year (1854) Wenrong's army was defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1854 Wenrong's army was defeated and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 崇綸自請出剿，謀脫身走避，文宗燭其隱，不許。

translations.literal: Chong Lun volunteered to go suppress but planned to slip away; the emperor saw through him and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Lun volunteered to take the field but meant to escape; the emperor saw through him and refused.

sentences.zh: 會丁憂，青麟代之，仍命崇綸留湖北協防。

translations.literal: When mourning duty fell on him, Qing Lin replaced him, yet Chong Lun was still ordered to stay in Hubei to assist defense.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning, Qing Lin replaced him, but Chong Lun was still ordered to remain in Hubei to help defend.

sentences.zh: 又以病乞罷，上怒，褫其職。

translations.literal: He again pleaded illness to resign; the emperor grew angry and stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: He again pleaded illness to resign; the emperor was furious and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 六月，武昌陷，崇綸先一日出走，徑往陝西。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Wuchang fell; Chong Lun had fled the day before and went straight to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Wuchang fell; Chong Lun had fled the day before and went straight to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 及曾國籓論劾，命逮治。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan memorialized against him, he was ordered arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan impeached him, he was ordered arrested and tried.

sentences.zh: 服毒自盡，以病故聞。

translations.literal: He took poison and died; it was reported as death from illness.
translations.idiomatic: He took poison and killed himself; his death was reported as due to illness.

sentences.zh: =何桂清=何桂清，字根雲，雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: He Guiqing, styled Genyun, was a native of Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He Guiqing (style name Genyun) was from Kunming, Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in Daoguang 15 (1835), entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in 1835, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷贊善，直南書房。

translations.literal: He was promoted to tutor and served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to tutor and served in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 五遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached grand secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he reached grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢兵部侍郎，以憂去，服闋，補原官，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year (1848) he was made vice minister of War; he left on mourning, and after mourning ended resumed his post then transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he was made vice minister of War; he left on mourning, and after mourning resumed his post and transferred to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In Xianfeng 2 (1852) he became Jiangsu education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he became Jiangsu education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 粵匪擾江南，桂清疏陳兵事，劾疆吏巽耎僨事，侃侃無所避，文宗奇之。

translations.literal: When Cantonese rebels disturbed Jiangnan, Guiqing memorialized on military affairs, impeaching frontier officials for being compliant and soft and ruining affairs—speaking bluntly without avoidance—and Wenzong marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping rebels ravaged Jiangnan, Guiqing wrote on military affairs, impeaching frontier officials for timidity and failure—speaking bluntly without fear—and Emperor Wenzong took notice.

sentences.zh: 四年，調倉場侍郎，旋授浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year (1854) he was transferred to grain transport vice minister, then soon appointed Zhejiang governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he was transferred to grain transport vice minister, then soon made Zhejiang governor.

sentences.zh: 自賊踞江寧，東南震動。

translations.literal: Since the rebels held Jiangning, the southeast was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels held Nanjing, the southeast was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 安徽徽州、寧國二府為浙江屏蔽，桂清嚴防要隘，別遣一軍屯守黃池，扼蘇、浙之衝，賊來犯，會提督鄧紹良擊卻之。

translations.literal: Huizhou and Ningguo prefectures in Anhui were Zhejiang's shield; Guiqing strictly guarded key passes, sent another army to garrison Huangchi to choke the Jiangsu-Zhejiang corridor, and when rebels came the regional commander Deng Shaoliang beat them off.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhou and Ningguo in Anhui shielded Zhejiang; Guiqing sealed the key passes, posted another force at Huangchi to block the Jiangsu-Zhejiang corridor, and when rebels attacked, regional commander Deng Shaoliang drove them back.

sentences.zh: 五年，檄道員徐榮勦賊黟縣、石埭，戰頗利，賊眾大至，徽勇潰走，榮眾寡不敵，遂戰歿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year (1855) he ordered circuit intendant Xu Rong to suppress rebels in Yi and Shitai counties with initial success; rebel numbers swelled greatly, Huizhou militia routed, Rong was outnumbered and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he ordered circuit intendant Xu Rong to fight rebels in Yi and Shitai with early success; rebel numbers surged, Huizhou militia broke, and outnumbered, Rong fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 桂清因言徽、浙脣齒，宜主客一心，事乃濟。

translations.literal: Guiqing thus said Huizhou and Zhejiang were lip and teeth—host and guest must be of one mind for affairs to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing argued that Huizhou and Zhejiang were interdependent—host and guest had to act as one before affairs could succeed.

sentences.zh: 疏入，諭戒地方官吏不分畛域。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, an edict warned local officials not to divide spheres.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the court warned local officials not to draw jurisdictional lines.

sentences.zh: 時賊陷徽州各屬，桂清檄知府石景芬、副將魁齡等，攻复徽州府城及休寧，分佈所部於昌化、於潛、淳安，杜賊來路。

translations.literal: When rebels took Huizhou's dependencies, Guiqing ordered prefect Shi Jingfen, vice commander Kui Ling, and others to recover Huizhou city and Xiuning and deploy forces at Changhua, Yuqian, and Chun'an to block rebel routes.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels overran Huizhou's counties, Guiqing ordered prefect Shi Jingfen, vice commander Kui Ling, and others to retake Huizhou city and Xiuning and post troops at Changhua, Yuqian, and Chun'an to cut rebel routes.

sentences.zh: 安徽巡撫時移駐廬州，徽、寧二郡懸絕江南，不能遙制，命桂清兼轄之。

translations.literal: The Anhui governor had moved his seat to Luzhou; Huizhou and Ningguo hung isolated south of the Yangzi and could not be controlled from afar, so Guiqing was ordered to take jurisdiction over them.
translations.idiomatic: The Anhui governor had moved to Luzhou; Huizhou and Ningguo lay cut off south of the Yangzi and could not be governed from afar, so Guiqing was ordered to take them under his charge.

sentences.zh: 江西賊侵入浙境，陷開化，犯遂安，桂清檄鄧紹良等合擊之，賊退徽境。

translations.literal: Jiangxi rebels invaded Zhejiang, took Kaihua, and attacked Su'an; Guiqing ordered Deng Shaoliang and others to join attack and rebels retreated to Huizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi rebels invaded Zhejiang, took Kaihua, and attacked Su'an; Guiqing ordered Deng Shaoliang and others to strike together, and the rebels withdrew into Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 週天受、石景芬等連复黟縣、石埭。

translations.literal: Zhou Tianshou, Shi Jingfen, and others successively recovered Yi and Shitai counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tianshou, Shi Jingfen, and others retook Yi and Shitai in succession.

sentences.zh: 桂清疏請添改鎮道員缺，俾專責成，以石景芬為徽寧池太道；

translations.literal: Guiqing memorialized to add and reform circuit and prefect posts for dedicated responsibility—appointing Shi Jingfen as Huining-Chitai-Taiping intendant;
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing asked to add and revise circuit and prefect posts so duties were clear, appointing Shi Jingfen intendant of Huizhou, Ningguo, Chizhou, and Taiping;

sentences.zh: 豫祺為總兵，不得力，復以江長貴易之。

translations.literal: Yu Qi as regional commander proved ineffective and Jiang Changgui replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qi as regional commander proved ineffective, and Jiang Changgui replaced him.

sentences.zh: 又用桂清議，命前侍郎張芾駐皖南治團練，督辦徽、寧防務，尋命兼顧浙江衢、嚴兩郡，與桂清協力製賊。

translations.literal: Following Guiqing's plan, former vice minister Zhang Fen was stationed in southern Anhui to organize militia and supervise Huizhou-Ningguo defense, soon also overseeing Zhejiang's Qu and Yan prefectures with Guiqing to contain rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Following Guiqing's plan, former vice minister Zhang Fen was posted to southern Anhui to organize militia and oversee Huizhou-Ningguo defense, soon also covering Zhejiang's Qu and Yan prefectures to work with Guiqing against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 六年，檄鄧紹良、秦如虎、都興阿等合攻寧國，別遣江長貴擊敗贛賊之襲太平者，連捷，克寧國府城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year (1856) he ordered Deng Shaoliang, Qin Ruhu, Du Xing'a, and others to jointly attack Ningguo; separately Jiang Changgui defeated Gan rebels raiding Taiping with successive victories and retook Ningguo prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 he ordered Deng Shaoliang, Qin Ruhu, Du Xing'a, and others to attack Ningguo together; separately Jiang Changgui defeated Jiangxi rebels raiding Taiping, won repeatedly, and retook Ningguo city.

sentences.zh: 朝廷益嘉桂清，思大用之。

translations.literal: The court praised Guiqing more and thought to employ him on a larger scale.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised Guiqing ever more highly and planned to give him greater responsibility.

sentences.zh: 杭州知府王有齡最為桂清倚用，擢權運、臬兩篆，為通判徐徵訐控。

translations.literal: Hangzhou prefect Wang Youling was Guiqing's most relied aide—promoted to act transport and judicial commissions—but was impeached by subprefect Xu Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou prefect Wang Youling was Guiqing's closest aide; he was promoted to act transport and judicial commissioner but was impeached by subprefect Xu Zheng.

sentences.zh: 桂清覆奏，辭悻悻，被詰責。

translations.literal: Guiqing's reply memorial was resentful and he was reproved.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing's reply was bitter in tone and he was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 遂以病乞罷，詔慰留之。

translations.literal: He then pleaded illness to resign; an edict comforted him and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness to resign; an edict comforted him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 會兩江總督怡良解職，文宗以籌餉事重，難其人，大學士彭蘊章薦桂清餉徽軍無缺，可勝任。

translations.literal: When Liangjiang governor-general Yi Liang was removed, Wenzong found provisioning difficult to replace—Grand Secretary Peng Yunzhang recommended Guiqing supplied Huizhou army without shortfall and could bear the duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangjiang governor-general Yi Liang was dismissed, Emperor Wenzong found provisioning hard to replace; Grand Secretary Peng Yunzhang recommended Guiqing, who had kept Huizhou's army supplied without shortfall and could fill the post.

sentences.zh: 七年春，命以二品頂戴署兩江總督，尋實授。

translations.literal: In spring of the seventh year (1857) he was ordered with second-rank rank button to act as Liangjiang governor-general, soon confirmed in the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1857 he was ordered to act as Liangjiang governor-general with second-rank rank button, and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 力荐王有齡，擢任江蘇布政使，專倚餉事。

translations.literal: He strongly recommended Wang Youling, promoted him Jiangsu provincial treasurer, and leaned on him wholly for provisioning.
translations.idiomatic: He strongly recommended Wang Youling, made him Jiangsu provincial treasurer, and relied on him entirely for supplies.

sentences.zh: 江寧久為賊窟，總督駐常州，軍事由將軍和春主之，而提督張國樑為幫辦，前督怡良但任運饋而已。

translations.literal: Jiangning long rebel nest; the governor-general quartered at Changzhou with Prince He Chun overseeing military affairs and regional commander Zhang Guoliang assisting—former governor Yi Liang only handled transport and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing had long been a rebel stronghold; the governor-general stayed at Changzhou while Prince He Chun directed military affairs and regional commander Zhang Guoliang assisted—former governor Yi Liang had handled only transport and supplies.

sentences.zh: 桂清屢疏陳方略稱旨，諭飭和春和衷商酌。

translations.literal: Guiqing memorialized strategy repeatedly to imperial pleasure; an edict urged He Chun to consult harmoniously.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing's repeated strategy memorials pleased the throne; an edict urged He Chun to consult with him in good faith.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，克鎮江，以濟餉功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: That winter Zhenjiang was taken and for provisioning merit he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhenjiang was recovered; for his work on supplies he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十年春，又因克九洑洲，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: In spring of the tenth year (1860) for taking Jiufuzhou he was promoted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1860, for retaking Jiufuzhou, he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 桂清意氣發舒，倚畀益重，甚負時望。

translations.literal: Guiqing's spirit expanded; reliance on him grew heavier and he bore great contemporary expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing's confidence soared; the court leaned on him ever more, and he bore great public expectations.

sentences.zh: 大軍屢捷，合圍江寧，賊勢窘蹙，四出求援。

translations.literal: The great army won repeatedly and besieged Jiangning; rebels were cornered and sought aid in every direction.
translations.idiomatic: The main army won repeatedly and besieged Nanjing; the rebels were hard pressed and sent out for help in every direction.

sentences.zh: 偽忠王李秀成乃謀竄浙，分大軍之勢，由安徽廣德徑趣杭州。

translations.literal: The False Loyal King Li Xiucheng planned to slip into Zhejiang to divide the great army—from Guangde in Anhui he pressed straight on Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Loyal King Li Xiucheng planned to slip into Zhejiang and divide the main force; from Guangde in Anhui he drove straight on Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 倉猝城陷，惟將軍瑞昌守駐防內城未下，詔促桂清、和春遣軍速援。

translations.literal: The city fell in haste; only General Ruichang held the garrison inner city unlost; an edict urged Guiqing and He Chun to dispatch troops at once.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell in sudden assault; only General Ruichang still held the inner garrison quarter; an edict urged Guiqing and He Chun to send troops at once.

sentences.zh: 於是檄提督張玉良率兵馳赴，至則內外夾擊，賊遽走。

translations.literal: He then ordered regional commander Zhang Yuliang to rush troops; when he arrived inner and outer forces attacked together and rebels fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered regional commander Zhang Yuliang to rush troops; when he arrived the garrison and relief force struck together and the rebels fled at once.

sentences.zh: 臨安、孝豐、安吉諸城相繼复。

translations.literal: Lin'an, Xiaofeng, Anji, and other cities were recovered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an, Xiaofeng, Anji, and other towns were recovered in turn.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉桂清功，予優敘。

translations.literal: An edict praised Guiqing's merit and granted preferential promotion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Guiqing's achievement and granted him preferential promotion.

sentences.zh: 時賊已圍金壇，陷江陰，遣總兵馬得昭、熊天喜、曾秉忠，副將劉成元水陸分路禦賊，兵分益單。

translations.literal: Rebels had besieged Jintan and taken Jiangyin; he sent generals Ma Dezhao, Xiong Tianxi, Zeng Bingzhong, and vice commander Liu Chengyuan by land and water to resist rebels, yet forces grew thinner as they were divided.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels had besieged Jintan and taken Jiangyin; he sent generals Ma Dezhao, Xiong Tianxi, Zeng Bingzhong, and vice commander Liu Chengyuan by land and water to hold them off, but his forces grew ever thinner as they were split.

sentences.zh: 賊乃合眾十餘萬出建平、東壩，一由東壩趨江寧，一由溧陽窺常州，桂清聞之，幾失所措。

translations.literal: Rebels then massed over a hundred thousand from Jianping and Dongba—one column toward Jiangning from Dongba, one toward Changzhou from Liyang—and Guiqing heard it and nearly lost his composure.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then massed over a hundred thousand from Jianping and Dongba—one column from Dongba toward Nanjing, one from Liyang toward Changzhou—and Guiqing, hearing this, nearly lost his composure.

sentences.zh: 會馬得昭、週天孚分援蘇、常，賊已趨金壇，陷句容。

translations.literal: When Ma Dezhao and Zhou Tianfu split to aid Suzhou and Changzhou, rebels had already pressed on Jintan and taken Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Dezhao and Zhou Tianfu split to aid Suzhou and Changzhou, the rebels had already moved on Jintan and taken Jurong.

sentences.zh: 句容為大營後路，自此隔絕。

translations.literal: Jurong was the great camp's rear route; from this it was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Jurong was the main camp's supply line; from then on it was cut off.

sentences.zh: 張玉良回軍抵常州，和春飛檄調援大營，桂清留勿遣，復調馬得昭，亦莫之應。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang returned to Changzhou; He Chun urgently summoned aid for the great camp but Guiqing detained him; he also called Ma Dezhao who likewise would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang returned to Changzhou; He Chun urgently ordered him to the main camp, but Guiqing kept him back; he also summoned Ma Dezhao, who likewise would not come.

sentences.zh: 王有齡已擢浙江巡撫，貽書桂清戒勿離常州一步，且曰：「事棘時危，身為大臣，萬目睽睽，視以動止。

translations.literal: Wang Youling had been promoted Zhejiang governor and wrote Guiqing warning never to leave Changzhou a step, saying: "Affairs are dire and peril extreme; as a great minister every eye watches—your movements are the gauge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youling had been made Zhejiang governor and wrote Guiqing warning him never to leave Changzhou, saying: "Affairs are desperate and peril extreme; as a senior minister every eye is on you—your movements set the measure.

sentences.zh: 一舉足則人心瓦解矣。」

translations.literal: One foot moved and popular resolve would collapse."
translations.idiomatic: One step away and morale would collapse."

sentences.zh: 蓋規之也。

translations.literal: This was to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: This was meant to counsel him.

sentences.zh: 會大雨雪，大營兵凍餒，索餉不得，乃譟亂，相率盡潰。

translations.literal: When heavy rain and snow fell, great camp soldiers froze and starved, could not get pay, and clamored in mutiny until all routed together.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain and snow came; the main camp's troops froze and starved, could not get pay, mutinied, and routed en masse.

sentences.zh: 和春、張國樑退守丹陽。

translations.literal: He Chun and Zhang Guoliang fell back to defend Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun and Zhang Guoliang fell back to defend Danyang.

sentences.zh: 桂清疏陳：「丹陽以上軍務，和春、張國樑主之；

translations.literal: Guiqing memorialized: "Military affairs from Danyang upward are He Chun's and Zhang Guoliang's;
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing wrote: "Military affairs from Danyang northward are He Chun's and Zhang Guoliang's;

sentences.zh: 常州軍務，臣與張玉良主之。」

translations.literal: Changzhou military affairs are mine and Zhang Yuliang's."
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou's military affairs are mine and Zhang Yuliang's."

sentences.zh: 部署稍定，即進規溧陽，而賊已迳犯丹陽，國樑死之，和春奔常州，桂清大驚。

translations.literal: When deployment settled slightly he advanced on Liyang, but rebels had already struck Danyang directly—Guoliang died and He Chun fled to Changzhou; Guiqing was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Once his dispositions were set he moved on Liyang, but the rebels had already struck Danyang—Guoliang was killed, He Chun fled to Changzhou, and Guiqing was badly shaken.

sentences.zh: 總理糧台查文經等希其意，請退保蘇州。

translations.literal: Grain transport commissioner Cha Wenjing and others guessed his mind and asked to fall back to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grain commissioner Cha Wenjing and others, reading his mind, urged him to fall back to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 桂清即疏陳軍事付和春，自駐蘇州籌餉。

translations.literal: Guiqing memorialized to hand military affairs to He Chun and himself quarter at Suzhou to provision.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing memorialized to hand military affairs to He Chun while he himself stayed at Suzhou to handle supplies.

sentences.zh: 將行，常州紳民塞道請留，從者槍擊，死十餘人，始得脫。

translations.literal: As he was leaving Changzhou gentry blocked the road begging him to stay; followers fired guns killing over ten before he could break free.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, Changzhou gentry blocked the road begging him to stay; his escort fired on the crowd, killing more than ten, before he could break through.

sentences.zh: 張玉良留守，尋亦走。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang stayed to defend but soon fled too.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang stayed to defend the city but soon fled as well.

sentences.zh: 士民登陴，數日城陷，屠焉。

translations.literal: Soldiers and people climbed the walls; within days the city fell and was slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and townspeople manned the walls; within days the city fell and was put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 桂清至蘇州，巡撫徐有壬拒勿納，疏劾其棄城喪師狀。

translations.literal: Guiqing reached Suzhou but Governor Xu Youren refused him entry and memorialized impeaching his abandoning the city and losing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing reached Suzhou, but Governor Xu Youren refused him entry and memorialized impeaching him for abandoning the city and losing the army.

sentences.zh: 和春退至無錫，傷殞。

translations.literal: He Chun retreated to Wuxi and died of wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun retreated to Wuxi and died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 桂清託言借外兵，遂之上海。

translations.literal: Guiqing pleaded borrowing foreign troops and went to Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing claimed he would borrow foreign troops and went to Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 蘇州亦陷，有壬殉之，遺疏再劾桂清，詔褫職逮京治罪。

translations.literal: Suzhou also fell; Youren died in loyalty and in a dying memorial again impeached Guiqing; an edict stripped his rank and ordered him taken to the capital for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou also fell; Youren died defending it and in a dying memorial again impeached Guiqing; an edict stripped his rank and ordered him brought to the capital for trial.

sentences.zh: 會各國聯軍犯京師，車駕幸熱河，遷延兩年。

translations.literal: When allied armies of various nations attacked the capital the court went to Rehe and delay stretched two years.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies attacked Beijing the court fled to Rehe, and proceedings dragged on for two years.

sentences.zh: 王有齡及江蘇巡撫薛煥皆其故吏，疊疏為乞恩，不許。

translations.literal: Wang Youling and Jiangsu Governor Xue Huan were both his former subordinates and memorialized again and again begging mercy—refused.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youling and Jiangsu Governor Xue Huan, both former subordinates, memorialized repeatedly begging mercy—but were refused.

sentences.zh: 言官數劾奏，同治元年，始就逮下獄，讞擬斬監候。

translations.literal: Censors impeached repeatedly; in Tongzhi 1 (1862) he was at last taken and imprisoned; judgment proposed suspended execution.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached him repeatedly; in 1862 he was at last arrested and imprisoned; the verdict proposed death with reprieve.

sentences.zh: 大學士祁俊藻等十七人上疏論救，尚書李棠階力爭，讞乃定。

translations.literal: Seventeen grand secretaries including Qi Junzao memorialized to plead; Minister Li Tangjie argued forcefully and the judgment was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen grand secretaries including Qi Junzao memorialized in his defense; Minister Li Tangjie argued forcefully, and the verdict was settled.

sentences.zh: 桂清援司道禀牘為詞，下曾國籓察奏。

translations.literal: Guiqing cited circuit and prefect petitions as his defense; the case was sent down to Zeng Guofan for investigation and report.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing cited memorials from circuit and prefect officials in his defense; the case was referred to Zeng Guofan for investigation.

sentences.zh: 國籓疏言：「疆吏以城守為大節，不宜以僚屬一言為進止。

translations.literal: Guofan memorialized: "Frontier officials take holding the city as the paramount principle—it should not hinge on one subordinate's word.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan wrote: "Frontier officials' paramount duty is to hold the city—a governor should not stay or flee on one subordinate's word alone.

sentences.zh: 大臣以心跡定罪，不必以公禀有無為權衡。」

translations.literal: Great ministers are judged by intent and conduct—not by whether a public petition exists or not as the measure."
translations.idiomatic: A senior minister is judged by intent and conduct—not by whether a public petition exists."

sentences.zh: 是冬，遂棄市。

translations.literal: That winter he was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was executed in public.

sentences.zh: 桂清由侍從出任疆事，才識明敏。

translations.literal: Guiqing from attendant service went out to frontier duty with clear sharp talent.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing rose from court service to frontier posts with clear, sharp talent.

sentences.zh: 在兩江值英吉利構釁，迭陳應付之策。

translations.literal: In Liangjiang when England provoked conflict he submitted policies repeatedly for coping.
translations.idiomatic: In Liangjiang, when Britain provoked conflict, he submitted policy after policy on how to respond.

sentences.zh: 偕大學士桂良等議稅則，多中肯綮，亦不能盡用其言。

translations.literal: With Grand Secretary Gui Liang and others he discussed tax schedules—many points hit the mark—yet his words could not all be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: With Grand Secretary Gui Liang and others he debated tax schedules; many of his points were sound, yet not all his advice was followed.

sentences.zh: 晚節敗裂，誤國殄民，雖廷議多有袒之者，卒難撓公論云。

translations.literal: His late career shattered disaster on the state and people; though court debate had many who sheltered him, in the end public opinion could not be turned.
translations.idiomatic: His late career collapsed in disaster for the state and people; though many at court spoke in his defense, public opinion could not finally be swayed.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：陸建瀛、何桂清皆以才敏負一時之望，膺江表重寄。

translations.literal: Commentary states: Lu Jianying and He Guiqing both bore contemporary hopes with quick talent and received heavy trust on the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Lu Jianying and He Guiqing both won their age's hopes with quick talent and were given heavy charge on the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 建瀛當軍事初起，不能預有規畫，​​臨事倉皇。

translations.literal: Jianying when military affairs first arose could not plan ahead and at the crisis acted in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Jianying, when war first broke out, could not plan ahead and acted in panic when crisis came.

sentences.zh: 桂清無料敵之明，又失效死之節。

translations.literal: Guiqing lacked the discernment to gauge the enemy, and again failed the integrity of dying for one's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing lacked foresight about the enemy and failed the duty of dying with his post.

sentences.zh: 二人者身名俱隕，罪實難辭。

translations.literal: Both men lost life and reputation alike; their guilt truly could not be excused.
translations.idiomatic: Both men ruined their lives and reputations; their guilt was beyond dispute.

sentences.zh: 青麟受事於危急之秋，艱難支拄，終以越境被誅，論者猶有恕詞焉。

translations.literal: Qing Lin took office in a season of crisis, braced himself through hardship, yet in the end was executed for crossing borders; commentators still had words of forgiveness for him.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Lin took office in desperate times and struggled to hold on, yet was executed for fleeing across borders; even so, commentators still spoke of him with some forgiveness.
